geographic_scope: Statewide at qualifying critical infrastructure facilities
status: Current / in force; enacted penalty amendment not yet effective
uas_topic: Critical infrastructure; overflight; contact; interference; consent; penalties
regulated_party: Any unmanned-aircraft operator near a qualifying critical infrastructure facility
regulated_activity: Operating below 400 feet over, contacting, interfering with, or disturbing a qualifying facility
requirement_type: Prohibition with government, owner, contractor, consent, and authorized-commercial exceptions
permit_or_approval_required: Prior written facility or property consent, qualifying contractual authority, or applicable FAA commercial authorization can satisfy an exception
summary: Oklahoma prohibits intentional or knowing unmanned-aircraft operation below 400 feet AGL over a qualifying critical infrastructure facility, physical contact with the facility or persons or objects there, and proximity close enough to interfere with or disturb operations. Covered facilities include specified energy, utility, water, telecommunications, industrial, freight, pipeline, and dam assets when fenced or appropriately posted. Exceptions include government and law-enforcement activity, facility or property owners, their contractors, prior written consent, and commercial UAS operations authorized by the FAA over that airspace. Current law allows civil damages; effective November 1, 2026, S.B. 1441 also subjects violations to § 21-1792.

geographic_scope: Statewide private property and places with a reasonable expectation of privacy
source_title: Unlawful use of drones for surveillance, recording, or unauthorized landing
uas_topic: Privacy; surveillance; eavesdropping; private property; landing
regulated_activity: Surveillance, photography, recording, observation, device installation, or landing involving private property
requirement_type: Intent-based prohibitions with limited business, government, and emergency exceptions
permit_or_approval_required: Owner or lessee consent is required for intentional landing; lawful authorization may otherwise apply
summary: Section 1743 makes it a misdemeanor to use a UAS or drone, except as authorized by law, to enter private property or airspace below 400 feet with intent to eavesdrop or surveil; install or use an unauthorized observing or recording device on private property; intentionally photograph, record, or observe a person where that person reasonably expects privacy; or intentionally land on private land or water belonging to another person without owner or lessee consent. The privacy-observation prohibition does not cover unintentional or incidental capture during a bona fide business or government purpose, and the landing prohibition excepts safety or emergency landings needed to avoid collision.
notes: Official Title 21 PDF pages 813-814. The bona fide business exception is limited to paragraph A(3) and unintentional or incidental observation; it does not create a general exception from the other prohibitions.

source_title: State park aircraft and drone permit rules
uas_topic: State parks; takeoff and landing; aircraft use; event permits
regulated_party: Any drone or aircraft operator using Oklahoma state park lands or waters
regulated_activity: Taking off, landing, or operating aircraft on state park lands or waters
requirement_type: Director-issued event permit or designated-location requirement
permit_or_approval_required: Yes — drone takeoff or landing requires a permit; other aircraft use is limited to designated locations or permit terms
summary: Oklahoma State Parks prohibits taking off or landing a drone unless authorized by permit. The aircraft rule also prohibits operating or using aircraft on park lands or waters outside locations designated by the State Parks Director or authorized by permit, bars powered-aircraft use within 500 feet of designated swimming beaches, boat docks, piers, or ramps, and requires compliance with FAA rules and state law. Drone usage is assigned to an Event Permit issued by the Director. Conducting a permit-required activity without a permit or violating permit conditions is prohibited and may result in suspension or revocation, removal from the park, and loss of related payments.
